notes:
Merged from two passes that agree on case 5 (critical, escalated for impact, description naming the packet drops), the notification 734 with article 227, the suggested link 528, the two critical SLA rows selected by case and definition, the stay on case 14, and all five dispositions (four kept, the case check repaired).
disagreement: value: requirement split on case 5: one pass tests the escalation and the priority as two requirements, the other as one; chose two because the request asks for the escalation and implies the priority raise in separate sentences, and each can fail on its own; the cells are the same either way.
disagreement: value: the case 14 stay: one pass also tests escalation_reason IS NULL, the other only priority and escalation; chose the tighter form because both hold on the seed.
disagreement: missing requirement: a stay that the retired article 195 is not linked to case 5 again; one pass has it, the other does not; kept because the policy links only published articles and 195 is the device's own article and the only one that mentions packet loss, so a loose search reaches it.
disagreement: missing requirement: a stay that no internal article is emailed on case 5; one pass has it, the other does not; kept because the policy makes internal articles visible to agents only and Elizabeth is a customer, so emailing one is forbidden.
disagreement: missing requirement: a stay on case 1; one pass has it, the other does not; kept because case 1 is Elizabeth's other open PA-3220 case, the row a loose reading of 'her case for this device' would sweep in, and it was logged as critical, not moderate.
No published article exists for product 128 itself: its one article (195) is retired, internal and already linked as applied. Article 227 (PA-3220 Variant 20, published, external) is kept as the benchmark's choice; article 244 (PA-3220 Variant 32, published, external) would fit the request equally well, and neither mentions packet drops.
The case's existing moderate SLAs (case_sla 9 and 10) are not tested: neither the request nor the policy says what becomes of them when the priority rises.
The policy asks for the escalation's justification in case notes, but the schema has no notes table. Entitlement validation is a read and gives no requirement.
